item.title: Eight US States Sue OpenAI Over ChatGPT Safety and Data Practices
item.description:
Eight US States Sue OpenAI Over ChatGPT Safety and Data Practices

OpenAI is facing a new wave of lawsuits from eight U.S. states that accuse the company of harming children and misleading customers about the safety of its ChatGPT chatbot.

🔍 Overview

  • The lawsuits were filed separately by Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho, and Montana.
  • Plaintiffs claim OpenAI put profits ahead of safety while developing ChatGPT.
  • The states allege violations of local consumer‑protection laws for failing to warn users about the chatbot’s dangers.

⚖️ Allegations

  • Misleading safety claims – OpenAI presented ChatGPT as a “safe, youth‑appropriate tool that puts safety first,” but the states say it is “dangerous to vulnerable users,” degrading critical thinking, encouraging paranoias and delusions, offering dangerous medical advice, and promoting unhealthy behaviors and relationships.
  • Data collection from minors – OpenAI is accused of gathering data from under‑age users and not doing enough to keep minors from accessing the chatbot.
  • Recklessness – The lawsuits cite recent rogue AI hacking incidents as evidence of OpenAI’s alleged recklessness.
  • Profit‑first mindset – Arizona’s filing states OpenAI has “devolved from its original mission … into a cautionary tale about what can happen when the development of a tool as powerful as AI is driven … by a profit‑at‑all‑costs mindset that sidelines essential safeguards.”

🛡️ OpenAI’s Response

  • In an emailed statement to The Verge, spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the company has “built industry‑leading age‑specific protections” into ChatGPT, including parental controls, break reminders, and age‑appropriate model protections.
  • OpenAI acknowledges that “no system can be perfect” and commits to working with experts to add more safeguards.
  • The company also says it is “committed to working with states on advancing pragmatic AI policies that apply to the entire AI industry – not just one company.”

📄 Legal Demands

  • The states are asking courts to impose civil penalties on OpenAI and to stop misleading the public about ChatGPT’s safety.
  • Some states are also seeking the deletion of unlawfully collected personal data.

💡 Why It Matters

  • The lawsuits represent a coordinated effort by multiple states to hold AI developers accountable for consumer‑safety and privacy concerns.
  • The outcomes could set precedents for how AI services are regulated, especially regarding protections for minors and transparency about risks.

Update (October 14): The OpenAI statement above was added to the coverage.

item.title: Florida Attorney General Seeks to Block OpenAI From Mimicking Human Attributes
item.description:
Florida Attorney General Seeks to Block OpenAI From Mimicking Human Attributes

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier is seeking a court order to block OpenAI from giving ChatGPT human attributes and developing new models without third-party approved safety guardrails. This follows a previous lawsuit filed by Florida regarding safety concerns.

⚖️ Legal Claims

Attorney General Uthmeier argues that OpenAI’s approach to engagement makes the bot potentially less trustworthy. His claims include:

  • Deceptive Personification: The use of first-person pronouns and output that mimics emotion suggests to users that the AI is a trustworthy “friend,” lulling them into a false sense of security.
  • Engagement Incentives: These attributes are used to increase engagement and contribute to OpenAI’s training data, encouraging users to rely on ChatGPT more.
  • Safety Concerns: Uthmeier has stated that OpenAI must “Stop calling it safe. Stop pretending it’s human. Stop selling it to kids.”

⚙️ Key Details

The legal filing includes specific requests and citations regarding AI development:

  • Safety Guardrails: Florida asks the court to block the development of new AI models unless they have “third-party approved safety guardrails.”
  • Evidence of Risk: The filing cites security incidents at Hugging Face, an Australian government website, and US government websites, as well as alarms raised by former OpenAI employees and researchers.
  • Youth Access: The claims follow the launch of “ChatGPT for Teens,” which OpenAI states includes default restrictions to ensure access reflects a user’s “developmental stage, reinforce real-world relationships, and support healthy use over time.”

💬 OpenAI Response

OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri stated that “People want to know AI is being developed safely, and that starts with what companies like ours do ourselves.” He provided the following updates:

  • Training Pause: OpenAI announced it has paused training its most capable models and will only resume when confident that additional safeguards are in place.
  • Policy Cooperation: Pusateri stated that governments have a role in setting safety standards and that OpenAI is committed to working with Florida and other states on pragmatic AI policies for the entire industry.

#OpenAI #ChatGPT #AISafety #Florida #AIRegulation

Source: Florida seeks a ban on ChatGPT acting like a person
